questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which action will NOT help reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding what to address first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To avoid accidents, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide what matters most. Always use your headlight to be visible. Keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do when riding at night?

options.text: Slow down.
Stay further back from the vehicle ahead.
Get closer to the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlight when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get closer to the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and stay further back from other vehicles. Use headlights of cars ahead to see the road. Use your high beam, unless another vehicle is coming toward you or ahead of you.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Ride where other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane away from oncoming traffic.
Move slowly up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is more noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle so drivers can see you as soon as possible. For example, at a blind corner to the right, ride on the left side of your lane so you are visible sooner.

questions.question: What should you do with your eyes when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused just ahead of your front tire.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your whole body to see through the turn.
Speed up before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Why should group riders avoid riding side-by-side?

options.text: A driver merging may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may block each rider's view.
Riding in pairs doesn't give riders enough room to move and avoid hazards.
Riders on the left can't exit the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs doesn't give riders enough room to move and avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists in a group should never ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough space to steer around hazards.

questions.question: A driver entering the highway may not see you. How can you help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
Move to the shoulder.
Weave in your lane to get the entering driver's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to make space for the merging driver.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms should hold you up on the bike.
You can reach the controls easily.
Your arms are straight when holding the grips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can reach the controls easily.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Don't stretch to reach the handgrips. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?

options.text: In a single-file line.
In a staggered line.
In pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best. But when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway, switch to single-file formation.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel locks up?

options.text: Keep holding the brake and the skid will stop.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and squeeze it again quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, let go of the front brake completely and right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Without signaling, so you don't distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing another vehicle on the left. Signal your intention, check for traffic, and pass only when it is safe. Signal again and return to your original lane when it is clear.

questions.question: When should you use a larger cushion of space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is usually appropriate. Use more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as when the road is icy or wet.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes right away.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually by closing the throttle, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road safely. Avoid braking, as this can also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips less than five miles long, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means the driver sees you.
Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
Guarantees the driver will yield to you.
May make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never depend on eye contact to ensure a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still do not notice them.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you must stop quickly on a slippery surface. The front brake is safe to use on wet pavement if you apply it slowly to avoid locking.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you, this:

options.text: Means that they see you.
Will never happen.
Does not mean they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never count on eye contact to guarantee that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to actually notice them.

questions.question: To help drivers merge safely from an entrance ramp into your lane, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to the next lane, if you can.
Not worry about it, since they are merging, not you.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane, if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them plenty of space by moving to a different lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, a horn:

options.text: Is useless.
Usually cannot be heard by other drivers.
Can quickly get someone's attention.
Should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is quieter than a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle in Colorado?

options.text: All riders
Riders under 18 years old
Riders who have had their license for less than two years
No riders are required to wear helmets

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders under 18 years old
questions.explanation: In Colorado, all riders and passengers under 18 must wear an approved helmet. All motorcycle riders should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handlebar
On the right handlebar

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press on the left handlebar
Always press on the right handlebar
Press on the handlebar opposite the direction of the turn
Press on the handlebar in the direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handlebar in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handlebar in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: Which formation keeps a group of riders closest together?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on the left, what part of your lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
Either the right or center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of your lane when passing. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.
